task: Fix EPMCDME-17100: marketplace unpublish/withdraw fails with ForeignKeyViolation because decide() writes an acting user.id with no users row into three FK columns; write only an existing user id or null, keep flag-True behaviour unchanged, and add a regression test.

key_reasoning.reason: MarketplaceQueueService.decide() is the single write path. It feeds three FK'd writes (assistants.marketplace_decided_by CAS, the mm_review_decision insert, and the activity_events actor via _snapshot_actor), plus the users-existence lookup through UserRepository. That is 2-3 components across the service and persistence layers. One fix inside decide() covers all six call sites, so the unpublish router probably needs no change.

The acceptance criteria are concrete, but the ticket names MARKETPLACE_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED=False as the trigger, and the code contradicts that: the missing users row comes from ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT=False or stand-in users. Two choices are still open: fix at the endpoint or inside decide(), and how the 'flag True unchanged' criterion applies, since the same failure also happens with the flag True.

Closest patterns are UserRepository.get_existing_user_ids and _snapshot_actor, and decide() already accepts decided_by_id=None. All FK columns are nullable, and the change needs no migration. Risk is held at M rather than S for three reasons: nulling only the CAS parameter moves the failure to the mm_review_decision FK at flush or commit; _snapshot_actor keeps an actor_id that has no users row, so the activity event is silently dropped; and the FK behaviour can only be observed with the real-PostgreSQL fixtures, which skip themselves when no database is reachable. Calibration: this sits at the S/M boundary next to bundled M example epmcdme-10203 (15). It stays S because it has fewer files and layers and no new endpoint.
